clue.text: Disorder guarantees pain for elderly person

indicators.note: used as a verb, to disorder letters is to jumble them out of their given sequence

parts.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Turmoil in later life brings guaranteed suffering for an old person.
explanation.definitionFit: A septuagenarian is someone in their seventies, which certainly counts as elderly.

clue.text: Supports inferior goods for short time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: backs a proposal or a person
second meaning: factory rejects sold cheaply
third meaning: brief moments, as in 'back in a few'

explanation.surface: Someone props up cheap rejects for a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: There are actually three meanings here, not two: a verb, a noun for flawed stock, and a noun for brief moments.
explanation.definitionFit: The one plural word covers seconding a motion, slightly flawed merchandise, and short instants of time.

clue.text: Writer's turned in this article to make a point

definitions.text: Writer's turned in this article to make a point

parts.note: surface reading: an author has handed in a piece of journalism
setter's reading: the writer is a pencil, rotated inside a small device that gives it a tip

explanation.surface: A journalist has submitted a piece in order to argue something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the pencil itself, 'turned' is the twisting motion, and 'article' is an object rather than a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: This stationery gadget is where a pencil gets twisted round to restore its pointed tip.

clue.text: Turn fifty, oddly lacking detachment

indicators.note: missing the odd-numbered positions means only the even-placed characters survive

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Reaching fifty, a person somehow lacks the old sense of distance.
explanation.definitionFit: In military usage a detachment is a body of troops sent off separately, that is, a unit.

clue.text: Frisk doctor going into prison

indicators.note: one item entering another ends up enclosed within it

parts.note: British spelling of jail
Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: A medic entering a jail gets searched by the guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' looks like a body search, but here it means to leap about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk and to gambol both mean to skip and caper about in high spirits, like lambs.

clue.text: E.g. German or Italian examination a linguist has included

indicators.note: the run of words contains the solution within itself, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: runs from inside the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A language test that a linguist has taken covers German or Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A German or Italian is a citizen of a particular country, that is, one of its nationals.

clue.text: Showing disloyalty, dismissing head? That's okay

indicators.note: sending away the head means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: amounting to betrayal of one's country

explanation.surface: A boss is fired for being disloyal, and that is considered acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reasonable is fair and acceptable, which is what calling it okay conveys.

clue.text: In which our conclusions are often non-U

definitions.text: In which our conclusions are often non-U

parts.note: surface reading: the way we finish things is often socially vulgar, 'non-U' meaning not upper-class
setter's reading: words ending in -our, like colour, drop the letter U in this variety of the language

explanation.surface: A snobbish remark that our endings are frequently common and lower-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' was a mid-century British label for speech thought lower-class; here it literally means 'without a U', as in color and honor.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US variety of the language, spellings like colour and favour lose their U to become color and favor.

clue.text: Shrub or tree, split by crack going upwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling upwards means reading from bottom to top
something split apart has another item wedged into the gap

parts.note: a common deciduous tree
to have a crack at something is to attempt it

explanation.surface: A bush or tree has been split by a crack running up its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrub or tree' reads as one definition, but only 'Shrub' defines; 'tree' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers, sacred to Venus in classical lore.

clue.text: Produce further evidence for swindle by company

parts.note: a con is a confidence trick
a business

explanation.surface: Investigators gather more proof of fraud committed by a business.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm a claim is to back it up with additional proof that it is true.

clue.text: Hear about old play that doesn't have happy ending

definitions.text: play that doesn't have happy ending

indicators.note: going around something places it on either side of it

parts.note: a judge hears a case, that is, tries it
elderly

explanation.surface: Listen to an old drama that ends sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the legal sense: to hear a case in court is to try it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a drama ending in disaster or death, the opposite of a comedy's happy close.

clue.text: Catch something that's over quick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to nab or arrest someone
second meaning: the horny plate that lies on top of the sensitive flesh at a fingertip

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like an adjective meaning brief, but it is a noun: the tender flesh under a fingernail.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a suspect is to catch them, and a fingernail covers the quick, the sensitive skin beneath it.

clue.text: Unrivalled businessman who plays game with board?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trader with exclusive control of a market
second meaning, playful: someone playing the property-trading board game

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a whimsical coinage from the board game's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who corners a market has no competitors; jokingly, a player of the famous property game fits too.

clue.text: Man following order put spies inside tank

indicators.note: something placed inside another is enclosed within it

parts.note: first part of a water tank, a cistern
the US intelligence agency
last letter of the same tank word

explanation.surface: An obedient man places secret agents inside a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a religious order, not a command; the Cistercians are a monastic order founded at Cîteaux.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cistercian is a monk belonging to that particular religious order, so he follows its rule.

clue.text: Bird is spotted, being in hide

indicators.note: something being inside another thing is enclosed by it

parts.note: first letter of skin, an animal's hide
taken as written
rest of skin, the animal's hide

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a bird from inside a hide.
explanation.walkthrough: A hide is a birdwatchers' shelter in the surface, but here it means skin; 'spotted' only dresses the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Computerised information turned a little mean

indicators.note: turned round, the phrase is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
low or ignoble

explanation.surface: Digital records have become slightly stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of data held on a computer.

clue.text: Toy first pair of children is holding not of the best quality

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, surrounded

parts.note: a spinning top is a toy
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening two characters of the following word are all that are kept

parts.note: opening pair of letters of the word

explanation.surface: A toy the first couple of kids hold is of poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP plus CH together hold NOT; the surface 'not of the best quality' tricks the solver into reading a negative definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal adjective for excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Republican in dissenting group that's vulgar or improper

indicators.note: something placed in a group sits within its members

parts.note: start of faction, a breakaway group within a party
standard abbreviation
rest of faction

explanation.surface: A Republican in a rebel wing behaves crudely or badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' and 'improper' sound like bad behaviour, but they are mathematical: a vulgar fraction is like 3/4, an improper one like 5/4.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic, vulgar (common) and improper fractions are two kinds of numerical ratio written as one number over another.

clue.text: For instance, losing ring — and in street, too — in part of Europe

indicators.note: losing items means they are taken away from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round like the letter
taken as written
abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An example loses a ring, also on a street, somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring, the word 'in' and the street abbreviation all come out of the opening phrase; 'and ... too' adds the last two to the list.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a country in western Europe, so it is a region of the continent.

clue.text: Record-holder emerging from tussle eventually

indicators.note: something emerging from words comes out of them, already present within

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A champion finally comes out of a struggle on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' suggests a champion athlete; it is a vinyl record's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A record sleeve is the card or paper cover that holds a vinyl disc.

clue.text: Hired as worker committed to union

definitions.meaning: first meaning: taken on as an employee
second meaning: betrothed, pledged to marry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union to go with the worker, but it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer engages staff, and a couple who are engaged have promised to marry.

clue.text: Drunk left in base, mostly

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, so its final letter goes
a thing placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: start of bottom, the base, shortened
standard abbreviation
rest of bottom without its last letter

explanation.surface: A drunk was left at the bottom of the heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk.

clue.text: Administer without a split, so it would seem

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, it means wrapping around another item

parts.note: start of apply, as in applying a remedy
taken as written
a tear or rip
rest of apply

explanation.surface: Give the treatment without any tear, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the archaic 'outside', so the verb surrounds the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently is a sentence adverb meaning as far as one can tell, so it would seem.

clue.text: Leaders in amateur game of golf eagerly excited

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the characters at their very front

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Amateurs leading a round of golf are thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes someone in a state of eager, impatient anticipation.

clue.text: Site for experiments set up on island, one in Asia

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means placed upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: laboratory
standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A research lab is established on an Asian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' looks like the definition but supplies the abbreviation I; 'one in Asia' defines, meaning one island there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island in south-east Asia, so it is one such island on that continent.

clue.text: Guilty person's argument against opposing one court

parts.note: pros and cons
versus
Roman numeral
abbreviation

explanation.surface: A prisoner's case against an opponent in a single court.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is someone found guilty of a crime and serving a sentence.

clue.text: Most of that section of party is becoming less hostile

indicators.note: only the greater part is taken, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word without its final letter
a faction within a political party

explanation.surface: Much of a political faction is starting to relax its opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations thawing is a metaphor from ice melting: becoming warmer and friendlier.

clue.text: Produced glossy cover for bilingual editor?

parts.note: speaking two languages, here those of France and Poland
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A dual-language editor produced a shiny dust-jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'bilingual editor' is a whimsical split of a woodworking term.
explanation.definitionFit: French polishing gives furniture a high-gloss shellac finish, so the wood has been given a shiny coating.
